sources.title: Drying-induced stress and deformation for clays: a numerical study of the problem
sources.locators: PDF pp. 3–5, 8–10 (0-based indices in web extraction); abstract, introduction, mechanical model
facts: Kaolin brick drying is modeled using moisture diffusion, shrinkage-dependent strains and elastic stress.
The abstract reports a cracking criterion maximum at the surface near a symmetry axis around 40 minutes, with an elevated initial risk period.
The mechanical model is explicitly a perfectly elastic approximation; moisture-dependent properties and missing viscoelastic data limit it.
sources.supports: Early moisture/shrinkage gradients can matter before a body's single lumped leather-hard threshold.
sources.doesNotVerify: No wind-pulse/recovery trial on coiled pots; no calibrated stress relaxation time or crack probability for island clay.

sources.title: Desiccation and Relaxation Regimes in Fracture of Drying Clay Films
sources.locators: PDF pp. 1–3 and 6; method, cracking sequence, limitations

conditions.material: Laponite RD and methanol suspension in a Petri dish
conditions.observations: Continuous mass loss and interval photographs of cracks

facts: Earlier rapid shrinkage produces large cracks; later narrow cracks are interpreted in terms of residual stress and particle rearrangement.
The experiment distinguishes different stages of crack development rather than one whole-body hardness threshold.
sources.doesNotVerify: Methanol film is not water-based coiled pottery; no validated coefficients for weather pulses, stress decay or spontaneous healing.
